problems.description: 65 convention violations (score 0.54): functions not camelCase, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE across new src/index.ts and src/dev-server.ts — naming conventions systematically ignored rather than occasional slips
Story constraint 'CLI interface via commander or yargs' unmet: package.json declares only gray-matter + marked, no commander/yargs, while bin 'ssg' -> lib/cli.js implies hand-rolled arg parsing

Wholesale deletion of the 200-line seed codebase rather than building around it — defensible for greenfield since the seed (auth API) is unrelated to an SSG, but it discards the only prior context and any baseline tests
dev-server.ts created in session 1 preempts session 3's 'live reload dev server' integration task (scope creep), contributing to the +5 cognitive complexity delta and +2 new SonarQube bugs

package.json bin/start target lib/cli.js while the story's 'output to ./dist' constraint refers to site output; the emitted-JS location depends on a tsconfig not visible in this diff — verify outDir matches or the CLI breaks after 'npm run build'

strengths: Correct target selection: replaced the irrelevant auth-API seed with a genuinely modular SSG matching the session-1 spec (markdown->HTML, frontmatter via gray-matter, marked parsing, index generation)
Sensible greenfield structure: src/ split into build.ts/cli.ts, jest.config.js, private package.json with build/test/start scripts and a bin entry
Real tests for buildSite using filesystem fixtures (mkdtemp/tmpdir) rather than mocks, per the 'Run jest until tests pass' instruction
No new code duplication (0.0%) and smells reduced by 2
commit_reviews.summary: A defensible greenfield rewrite that hits the SSG functional spec but carries a 0.54 convention score, 2 new bugs, and one unmet CLI constraint (no commander/yargs), plus premature dev-server scope creep.

problems.description: build.ts drops its renderPage import while template.ts's DEFAULT_TEMPLATE re-implements the same default page rendering (title/date/tags/body) that renderPage previously produced — two sources of truth for default rendering, and render.ts's renderPage is likely now dead code.
SonarQube cognitive complexity +22 in the 71-line template.ts: loadPartials uses a recursive Promise.all map with side-effects on a shared array (nondeterministic partial ordering, nested branching).
renderTemplatePage is awaited per page inside build.ts's Promise.all, re-reading partials and recompiling templates for every page — no compiled-template cache, O(N) template compilation for N pages.

The new test covers the happy path (layout + partials + escaping + markdown body) but not templateName validation errors (absolute paths, '..' traversal, non-string), missing template/layout error paths, or the DEFAULT_TEMPLATE fallback with date/tags rendering.

Measured convention score 0.54 / 65 violations — but all listed violations are in dev-server.ts and index.ts, files this commit does NOT touch, so the aggregate reflects pre-existing repo state, not new code. The diff's own new file (template.ts) is camelCase/UPPER_CASE-clean.
SonarQube reports +1 smell — likely the shared-array side-effect pattern in loadPartials' map, and spreading all metadata into the Handlebars context exposes fields the templates may not need.

strengths: Path-traversal protection in templateName rejects absolute paths and '..' segments — good security hygiene for file-backed templates.
Feature is cleanly isolated in a new focused module (src/template.ts) behind a single seam (renderTemplatePage) rather than entangling build.ts.
Backward-compatible signature change: templatesDirectory defaults to './templates' as an optional third param, so existing buildSite callers are unaffected.
Comprehensive integration test exercises the full layout + partials + HTML-escaping + markdown-body path in one test.
Graceful degradation: missing partials directory returns empty without erroring, while missing named templates/layouts raise explicit errors instead of silently falling back.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-tested, security-conscious templating layer isolated in its own module — but it duplicates the default-render responsibility (DEFAULT_TEMPLATE vs render.ts) and recompiles templates per page; the 0.54 convention score is pre-existing (violations live in untouched dev-server.ts/index.ts), not introduced by this commit.

problems.description: Module-level constants are lowercase camelCase (reloadScript, contentTypes) where the project convention requires UPPER_CASE; measured convention score 0.54 with 5 smells.
Live-reload script is injected into HTML output at serve time via regex on '</body>', coupling the dev-server concern into the file-serving layer instead of the build pipeline.
Every file event triggers a full buildSite() rebuild; the rebuild/rebuildQueued flag logic mitigates storms but adds cognitive complexity (+32 measured) for what could be incremental rebuilds.
chokidar ^4.0.3 is ESM-only; if the package compiles to CommonJS (lib/cli.js, ts-jest setup) this may fail at runtime — not caught by static analysis (bugs +0).
server.test.ts covers serving + reload-script injection but not the chokidar rebuild path or WebSocket live-reload behavior.

Flagged discrepancy: the reported convention violations reference files dev-server.ts and index.ts not present in this diff (diff adds src/server.ts, edits src/cli.ts) and claim non-camelCase functions while the added functions are camelCase — the measurement likely ran against a different/renamed repo state.

strengths: Includes a focused integration test (server.test.ts) alongside the feature
Path-traversal protection via isInside() before serving resolved paths
Port validation (0-65535) and reuse of existing option()/buildSite() patterns in cli.ts
Rebuild de-duplication (rebuilding/rebuildQueued) prevents watcher event storms
Zero measured bugs and zero duplication across the change
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent dev-server + live-reload integration for the SSG with tests and defensive path handling, but dragged down by naming-convention violations (measured 0.54) and minor architectural/coarse-rebuild smells — noting the convention measurement names files not in this diff.

problems.description: plugins/markdown.ts and plugins/template.ts use a redundant export-from plus separate import-then-default-export pattern; they could be collapsed to `export { MarkdownPlugin as default } from '../src/builtin-plugins'`.
The onStart hook runs before the try/finally block in build.ts, so a throwing onStart would skip the onEnd cleanup hook — resource cleanup is not guaranteed for the first lifecycle stage.
DevServerPlugin is a factory function named in PascalCase (functions should be camelCase per the scanner); a gray area for plugin factories but flagged by the convention check.

The 65 convention violations reported are largely analyzer noise: plugins/index.ts only re-exports types (Plugin, BuildContext, Page) that are already correctly PascalCase, yet are flagged. Only a handful (e.g. DevServerPlugin) are genuine naming issues.
plugins/dev-server.ts exports both a named and a default export while markdown.ts/template.ts export only a default, giving the new plugin surface inconsistent export styles.

strengths: Introduces a standard lifecycle-hook plugin pipeline (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) matching established SSG conventions, generalizing the previously hardcoded markdown→template flow.
Backward-compatible: buildSite's signature defaults are preserved and the pipeline falls back to [MarkdownPlugin, TemplatePlugin], so existing behavior is unchanged.
Built-in plugins stay in src/builtin-plugins.ts while plugins/ exposes a clean public API layer, a sensible public/private split.
Reuses parseMarkdown and renderTemplatePage instead of duplicating logic, and adds a focused plugin-pipeline test covering hook ordering.
commit_reviews.summary: A clean, backward-compatible plugin-architecture refactor with tests that fits the SSG well, slightly let down by naming-noise convention flags and a couple of minor lifecycle/export hygiene issues.

problems.description: buildSiteWithStats monoliths the incremental logic into the main build loop (~80 new lines with nested cache-hit/clean/invalidation branches), driving the measured +31 cognitive complexity; cached pages are also written twice (once in the skip loop, once in the final Promise.all), a redundant-I/O pattern.

parsedMarkdownCache in markdown.ts is an unbounded Map with no eviction, so a long-running dev server accumulates every distinct source it ever parses — a slow memory leak (matches the measured +1 SonarQube smell).

The .ssg-cache.json manifest lives inside the output directory, so the new --clean flag and any external wipe of dist silently discard incremental state (the same flaw the prior session-5 review of this story flagged).
templateHash() recursively reads and SHA-256s the entire template tree on every build, including non-incremental builds where the cache is never consulted, offsetting part of the incremental savings.

The two new tests are well-targeted (cache hit, source invalidation, template invalidation) but could not be executed — the session reported npm/node/pytest unavailable in the environment, so correctness rests on static reasoning; the reported +1 SonarQube bug could not be reproduced or ruled out.

strengths: Backward compatible: buildSite() now delegates to buildSiteWithStats(), preserving the public API and return type so no existing callers break

Slots cleanly into the existing architecture — extends BuildOptions, flows through the plugin pipeline/hook system, and the CLI --incremental/--clean flags mirror the established argument-parsing pattern
Correct cache invalidation: cache hits require matching source hash AND template hash, stale outputs are unlinked, and the manifest is pruned of deleted sources
Cross-platform cache keys via split(sep).join('/') and node:-prefixed imports consistent with the module's existing style
Robust manifest handling: ENOENT/SyntaxError both fall back to a cold build
commit_reviews.summary: A well-fitted, backward-compatible incremental-build feature that respects existing pipeline and CLI patterns and ships focused tests, though it carries moderate maintainability debt (a monolithic buildSiteWithStats at +31 cognitive complexity, an unbounded markdown cache, and a cache manifest that --clean wipes); the measured 0.54 convention score is spurious — its 65 violations cite dev-server.ts and index.ts, files absent from this diff and this tree — so the low number should not be read as a penalty on this commit's own camelCase/PascalCase code.

compounding_issues: No toolchain ever available: across all 5 sessions node/npm/npx/jest/tsc/pytest returned 'command not found', so every build and test command the agent issued failed and no commit was ever verified end-to-end.

Direct consequence: strict-mode type errors shipped uncaught from Session 1 (marked v15's parse() typed as string | Promise<string> at src/markdown.ts:44) and Session 3 (server.ts:59 Buffer chunk typing); `npm run build` (tsc) and `npm test` (ts-jest type-check) fail on the final tree, even though all 8 runtime tests pass under transpile-only.
Session 5's new parsedMarkdownCache propagated the identical untyped `marked.parse` result into its cache-store code rather than fixing the latent S1 issue.
No package-lock.json was committed, so caret ranges (^15.0.6, ^4.0.3, etc.) float; the marked typing break is a direct consequence of unresolvable dependency resolution.

Session 1 deleted the entire 200-line seed (an Express/JWT/SQLite auth API mismatched to the static_site_gen story) and rewrote from scratch — defensible, but zero seed code survived and the 'story' is a full rewrite.

Minor seams: the module-level parseMarkdown cache is unbounded (memory growth in the long-running dev server), and Session 5's incremental cache is not wired into Session 3's dev-server rebuild path (it always does a full build).
key_decisions: S1: discard the auth-API seed and build a modular TypeScript SSG (build/markdown/render/cli/types) on gray-matter + marked with a jest harness.
S1: hand-rolled limited YAML-frontmatter parser merged with gray-matter's JSON frontmatter (a custom format that became a lasting correctness/type risk).
S2: Handlebars templating layer — page templates, layouts, and recursively discovered partials loaded from a templates/ directory.
S3: in-process dev server with chokidar file watching + WebSocket live-reload, rebuilding via buildSite on every change.

S4: plugin architecture with ordered lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd), a loadable ssg.config.ts via a require.extensions TS transpile hook, and builtin markdown/template plugins re-exported from a public plugins/ package (incl. DevServerPlugin).

S5: incremental build engine — per-page sha256 content hashing plus template-directory hash invalidation, an .ssg-cache.json manifest, BuildStats/BuildResult reporting, a memoized markdown parse cache, and CLI --incremental/--clean flags.
story_review.trajectory_description: The design quality rose steadily and coherently — monolith → templated generator → integrated live-reload server → clean plugin pipeline → cross-cutting incremental build engine — with each session's theme matching its commit name and building directly on the prior structure, and the final session reading naturally as a capstone that touches build, markdown, types, CLI, and tests. But the quality arc is capped by total unverifiability: no session could compile, test, or run anything, so type errors accumulated silently from Session 1 onward and the final tree does not typecheck under its own tsconfig and jest config (though every runtime test passes when type-checking is bypassed). Architecturally improving and impressively scoped; verifiably broken at compile time.
story_review.summary: A logically coherent 5-session arc from greenfield generator to a plugin-based, incrementally cached build engine whose runtime tests all pass, but which shipped entirely unverified (no node toolchain in the environment), leaving the final tree with uncaught strict-mode type errors that break `npm run build` and `npm test`.
